title: Generic finite algebra splits after a finite separable field extension
statement: Let K be a field and C a finite-dimensional commutative K-algebra [def-pc-field-extension]. There exists a finite separable field extension K'/K such that the reduction of C tensor_K K' is a finite product of finite field extensions L_j/K', each L_j/K' purely inseparable [def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension].

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-over-zero-dim-local-discrete-spectrum] applied with the base field $K$ (a local ring whose only prime is $(0)$) and $B=C$, the ring $C$ has finitely many prime ideals $\mathfrak m_1,\dots,\mathfrak m_r$, each maximal, with $\mathfrak m_1\cap\dots\cap\mathfrak m_r=N:=\sqrt{(0)}$. Distinct maximal ideals are pairwise comaximal, so [lem-pc-crt-ideal-quotient-product] gives $C_{\mathrm{red}}=C/N\cong E_1\times\cdots\times E_r$ with $E_i=C/\mathfrak m_i$, a field which is finite over $K$ as a quotient of the finite-dimensional $C$ ($r=0$ when $C=0$). If $N^m=0$, then the image of $N\otimes_KK'$ in $C\otimes_KK'$ has $m$th power zero, and by right exactness of $-\otimes_KK'$ the quotient by it is $C_{\mathrm{red}}\otimes_KK'\cong\prod_i E_i\otimes_KK'$; hence $(C\otimes_KK')_{\mathrm{red}}\cong\prod_i(E_i\otimes_KK')_{\mathrm{red}}$, since an element of a finite product is nilpotent exactly when each component is nilpotent.

source.place: Algebra, Lemmas 00KH, 00E0 and 00DT: finite-dimensional algebra has finitely many maximal primes, nilradical their intersection, Chinese remainder

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-separable-split-purely-inseparable-residue-fields] to the finite extensions $E_1,\dots,E_r$ of $K$. It gives a finite separable field extension $K'/K$ such that every prime of each finite $K'$-algebra $K'\otimes_KE_i$ has residue field finite purely inseparable over $K'$.

source.place: Proof of More on Morphisms, Lemma 02LM, lines 12060-12079

proof.text: For each $i$, the finite $K'$-algebra $K'\otimes_KE_i$ has finitely many maximal ideals and nilradical equal to their intersection, by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-over-zero-dim-local-discrete-spectrum] with the base ring $K'$. The maximal ideals are pairwise comaximal, so [lem-pc-crt-ideal-quotient-product] identifies its reduction with the finite product of its residue fields. Each such residue field is finite purely inseparable over $K'$ by step 2.

source.place: Algebra, Lemmas 00E0 and 00DT, nilradical intersection and Chinese remainder theorem

proof.text: Taking the product over $i$ and using the last isomorphism of step 1 yields $(C\otimes_KK')_{\mathrm{red}}\cong\prod_jL_j$, where every $L_j/K'$ is finite purely inseparable. The extension $K'/K$ is finite separable by construction, which proves the statement.
